articles.content:
EXCLUSIVE: The resurgence of independent television series continues to grow with Justin Long ( Barbarian, You Deserve Each Other ) and Kate Bosworth ( Still Alice, Along for the Ride ) starring in The Renovation , a fully-financed indie comedy series. It hails from Lucas Carter ( Summer of '69) , Nick Kreiss ( Punk'd ) who directs all episodes, Intrigue , Script2Screen and Hammerstone Studios .

Production has wrapped in Los Angeles, and EPs Intrigue, Script2Screen and Hammerstone will begin shopping the series to streaming platforms and television networks this month for distribution. articles.title: Grammy Nominations Snubs and Surprises: Harry Styles, Madonna, Noah Kahan Miss Top Nods as Raye, Rosalía Overperform
articles.summary: Styles, who won album of the year with 'Harry's House' back in 2023, was completely shut out of the Grammy race this time, one of the most notable snubs this season.
articles.content:
It was less than four years ago that Harry Styles won the Grammy for album of the year, but he won't get a chance to defend his title or win another Grammy this go around for his latest album Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally , as he was completely shut out of the 2027 Grammy nominations .

Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally was a bit more sonically complex than Styles' past album of the year winner Harry's House , and heading into this year, Styles was widely looked at as a Grammy contender for his latest release, which debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 album chart while lead single “Aperture” hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. Neither the album nor the single had the same staying power as Harry's House or its lead single “As It Was,” though he gave the album more buzz with a 30-show Madison Square Garden residency as part of his Together, Together tour. Evidently, it wasn't enough to sway the Grammy voters. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Lady Gaga and Doechii's "Runway" Is Sole 'Devil Wears Prada 2' Song Oscar Submission (Exclusive) Music John Summit Blasts Grammys After Dance Snub: "It's All a F***ing Joke"

While Abrams scored a best new artist nomination in 2024, it's not her first time getting the Grammys ‘ cold shoulder, also failing to land expected song and record of the year nods last year for “That's So True.”

Others were lucky enough to score nominations but maybe not as many as pundits (or fans) had expected. For anyone else, five Grammy nominations is an incredibly impressive feat, but even though that's how many nods superstar singer-songwriter Taylor Swift received Monday — with noms in all three of the general categories — it's perhaps an understated showing compared to what we've come to expect for the world's biggest artist.

Speaking of superstar musicians, Paul McCartney was left out of the major categories for his latest release The Boys of Dungeon Lane , which only landed one nomination, for best traditional pop vocal album. articles.title: After 9 Years, Black Clover Finally Reveals Noelle's True Feelings for Asta
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Studio Pierrot Black Clover has been sitting on this one ever since the TV anime kicked off its run nearly a decade ago, but the newest episode of the second season has finally seen Noelle Silva accept her real feelings of love for Asta. Black Clover Season 2 has been working its way through the Spade Kingdom […]
articles.content:
After Noelle had lost to Vanica back in the first season of the series, Black Clover Season 2 has been able to show off the fruits of her mana training in the Heart Kingdom. This has made her stronger than ever before as she's been surviving thus far, and the latest episode of the series sees Noelle pushing beyond her limits once Asta arrives to help her . It's through seeing Asta in this situation that Noelle herself realizes that she really does love him as he's been able to get her back to her senses.

Black Clover Season 2 Episode 7 continues the fight against the Supreme Devil Megicula after she emerged from Vanica's body. Noelle and the others had hit a wall through the limits of her power, but Asta soon arrives to help with his anti-magic just in time to keep Megicula from killing Lolopechka with a suicidal magic explosion. This gives Noelle the hope she needed to keep going on, and it's in this moment that Noelle realizes what she has been fighting back against this whole time. Because while she was telling herself different, she really does love Asta.

Knowing that Asta had already been recklessly pushing beyond his own limits to even help in that moment, Noelle realizes that he's put his complete faith in her. In the moment she knows that just the fact that he came to save her at all, and just in thinking about Asta while she fights, it's enough for Noelle to push through for one final attack against Megicula. It's in this thought giving her strength that Noelle accepts her true feelings, and now moves forward with all of that in mind at last.

Noelle has been the third major character in the series along with Asta and Yuno as she's gotten plenty of development and improvement over all of the arcs thus far. This arc sees her become a Saint Stage level fighter with the use of Undine , and through that ability she's able to deal the final blow to the Supreme Devil. It's going to keep her in the action as everything continues to ramp up from here on out, but Asta's still going to be much further away than that.

We've only seen Asta show any kind of romantic interest in his childhood crush, Sister Lily, so it's unclear how he views Noelle or her romantic rival Mimosa Vermilion. He's been squarely focused on fighting and getting stronger, but their time together as Black Bulls has made Noelle a dear friend to Asta until now. We'll just have to see if Noelle actually acts on her feelings, so how do you feel about this development? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: As Bari Weiss Receives 60 Minutes Backlash, She’s Apparently Involved In Another CBS Show’s Drama
articles.summary: Another storied CBS News program is now making headlines.
articles.content:
Bari Weiss’ tenure as the editor-in-chief of CBS News has sparked a myriad of responses from media pundits and the general public, who’ve taken issue with the organization’s content. While Weiss has received praise in some circles, she’s also been critiqued for some of her decisions, including those made in regard to 60 Minutes . Even now, some continue to chastise her editorial and staffing choices for the news magazine show. All the while, it seems Weiss is embroiled in some reported drama involving another news program.

Although Brennan is still with the show, it just lost two key members of its team. Senior executive producer Mary Hager recently announced that she would depart CBS News after 25 years with the network. Another key detail about this move is that since 2022, Hager has served as the executive director of politics for the Eye Network and has overseen its Washington Bureau. FTN executive producer Anne Hsu is leaving the show but, unlike Hager, she’ll remain with CBS and will head up its Hong Kong bureau.

These major exits mark the end of another era for Face the Nation , which debuted back in 1954 and, as of right now, it’s unclear just how Weiss will proceed in regard to filling those posts. With this, the Free Press founder finds herself in another staffing situation just months after her overhaul of 60 Minutes . And that series of personnel changes is still being discussed as part of the backlash that 60 has received as of late.

Earlier this year, Anderson Cooper exited his correspondent post at 60 Minutes after nearly two decades, citing a desire to have more time to spend with his loved ones. It was subsequently reported, however, that Cooper’s departure was partially due to disagreements with Weiss. Shortly after Cooper’s move, Weiss and series EP Nick Bilton fired correspondents Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi along with former EP Tanya Simon and several others. Correspondent Scott Pelley was also fired days later after reportedly accusing Weiss of “murdering” the show .

articles.title: Mo Brings Plenty Hopes Real-Life Inspired 'Marshals' Episode Brings Justice to Late Nephew
articles.summary: The latest episode of the hit 'Yellowstone' spinoff — about the death of a Native family member that initially goes uninvestigated — was inspired by the untimely death of Mo's nephew, Cole Brings Plenty.
articles.content:
Mo Brings Plenty, his family and community have been rocked by the untimely death of Mo's nephew, 1923 actor Cole Brings Plenty. The 27-year-old was found dead in April 2024 after he had been reported missing . His death came between seasons one and two of the Yellowstone prequel, sparking his recasting ( with Jeremy Gauna ), a final season that honored his memory and now, an entire episode of Marshals inspired by what happened.

In Sunday's episode of Yellowstone ‘s hit CBS spinoff following Kayce Dutton ( Luke Grimes ), titled “Roughstock,” Mo, an enrolled member of the Lakota Nations who plays the right-hand man to Broken Rock Tribe chief Thomas Rainwater (Gil Birmingham) in both Yellowstone and Marshals, searches on horseback with Kayce (Grimes) for Mo's missing nephew (played by Will Strongheart), only to eventually find him dead, and a police department refusing to investigate the death. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Michelle Pfeiffer and Kurt Russell Tease Major "Twists" in Season 2 of 'The Madison' TV Luke Grimes Wasn't Sure If 'Marshals' Would Be a Hit. Now He's Prepping for a 'Yellowstone' Kind of Run

The storyline is ripped from what Mo believes happened to his real nephew. In Cole's case, the Lawrence Police Department in Kansas found no foul play involved, ruling that Cole acted alone and took his own life. Mo hasn't stopped pushing a different narrative ever since. “For his murder to go uninvestigated, and for it to be written off as ‘no foul play,' because they didn't want to invest anything into it? It's heartbreaking," he had told The Hollywood Reporter back in March . “We're not letting it go.”

Now that the episode has aired, Mo, who also works behind the scenes as the show's American Indian Affairs coordinator, talks again with THR below about the bravery of the Paramount Taylor Sheridan series and Marshals showrunner Spencer Hudnut to spotlight Cole's story on television, the emotions around reliving the tragedy of his nephew's death, and the justice he hopes the episode can help bring to murdered and missing Indigenous people. “This is for the injustice that occurs to American Indian people and the victims who are truly victims, who are being being labeled otherwise and not being taken seriously,” he says. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

This must be heavy for you, so thank you for speaking with me about the making of this episode inspired by your late nephew. Did you approach (showrunner) Spencer Hudnut about doing this, or did Spencer approach you?

It all began when my brother, Joe, Cole's father, and I were sharing the experience of what we were going through. Spencer mentioned something about it being up to us. Saying, "I know it's gonna be deep, and it's hard. But it's up to you." We said, we have to do it. Not just for the sake of remembrance or in honoring Cole, but for all the other cases, all the other families whose cases of their loved ones not being looked at or being taken seriously and just thrown away. It was very important. And I knew it was going to be doable because the cast and crew are an amazing group of people. They all understood and had the knowledge of what we've experienced and gone through.

Did you have to pitch this to the studio or network to get them on board?

I think that was on Spencer. Mad respect for Spencer; even doing so, is very important.

Did you talk to Taylor Sheridan about how to handle putting this storyline into the show?

No. I knew exactly what I wanted to do. My biggest thing was that I wanted to relay the true emotions and spirit of it all, even the frustrating moments. Because it's a roller coaster ride, and it still is today. It's still fresh in our minds, my family's minds, especially my brother Joel. He struggled. It was truly, truly a great loss for us. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Spencer wrote this episode. Did you collaborate?

Yes, he wrote it, and Spencer and the writing team are a great group of amazing, beautiful human beings. My brother and I went to the writers room early on, before the season even started, to spend a day with them. We talked about different things that go on within tribal councils, the political side of what goes on on a reservation, the non-political side of it and then, of course, we shared our experience of not talking about the MMIW (Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women) and MMIP (Missing and Murdered Indigenous People), but actually conveying what it's really like to have that experience. There are hundreds and hundreds of families who have their loved ones… murdered and missing; the disappearance of loved ones just being written off as nothing.

From my previous conversations with you , this episode is very close to what you believe happened to your nephew in real life. What was it like for you to film this beat by beat , playing an uncle who loses his nephew? [ Note: In the end of the episode, Kayce's team pushes for the police to investigate the death, opening up the storyline to continue .]

It was about doing justice. But it was also good to have Luke Grimes there, and Gil Birmingham, and the crew; individuals who understood and knew. Will [Strongheart], who portrayed [Mo's onscreen nephew] Troy, was very familiar. He came to Cole's funeral; they all knew what we were going through, especially for me. So it was easy to fall back into that space, because I knew there were others who would be there to help me if I needed it. But at the forefront of my mind was the injustice that occurs to American Indian people and the victims who are truly victims who are being being labeled otherwise and not being taken seriously. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

This is a big platform: Marshals is a mega-hit for Paramount. You will shine a light on this happening everywhere, but do you hope it moves the needle specifically with your nephew's case?

Unfortunately, the way I see it, if a police department doesn't want to investigate something then there's a connection. Bottom line, hands down. Outside of that, what I hope this episode achieves is that it will drive people who are non-Native, who are unfamiliar, to go down this journey.

We mentioned MMIW, MMIP, in the past — murdered and missing Indian women and people. But to actually have a storyline that will hopefully have the audience see it through Mo's, Kayce's, Rainwater's eyes? Just to be able to actually see what is going on. The positive side in this story is that law enforcement actually does get involved — the marshals, but not the police. There's a line where the sheriff said, "Ah, this happens all the time." I'm glad Spencer included that line because that's really, honestly, what a lot of families hear from law enforcement when when their loved ones are found.

After we spoke the last time, the Lawrence Police Department responded to our interview with a statement . Did you see what they said? [“ The entire case contains clear evidence that there was no foul play involved in Cole's death and that Cole acted alone ."]

Oh, yeah, of course. Out of respect for my family, I encouraged my brother, Joe, to seal the records. Little did we know that it was going to give them an out. What occurred in Cole's case, there were allegations. And they let go the people they should have interviewed to get the true answers. If the police department really doesn't want to investigate, then to me, that's every bit of proof that there's something to hide.

Harlan Coben has been on a tear at Netflix with his most recent, I Will Find You , becoming the streamer's fifth most popular series of all time.

Coben is back with limited series The Innocent , marking his 15th adaptation for Netflix. The streamer has greenlit the project, after Deadline revealed it was in development earlier this year.

The Innocent reunites Coben with Robert Hull, showrunner of I Will Find You , which starred Sam Worthington.

Hull launched production company StoryMath earlier this year with Bryan Wynbrandt and Steven Lilien, who created CBS' God Friended Me , and the company has now signed a new overall deal with Netflix. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

Interestingly, The Innocent has already been adapted by Netflix as Spanish series El Inocente in 2021.

The book follows Matt Hunter, who served nine years in prison after innocently trying to break up a fight-and ending up a killer. Now nine years after his release from prison, his innocence long forgotten, he's an ex-con who takes nothing for granted. With his wife Olivia pregnant and the two of them closing on a house in his hometown, things are looking up. Until the day Matt gets a shocking, inexplicable video call from Olivia's phone. And in an instant, the unraveling begins.

A mysterious man who begins tailing Matt turns up dead. A beloved nun is murdered. And local and federal authorities–including homicide investigator, Loren Muse, a childhood schoolmate of Matt's with a troubled past of her own–see all signs pointing to a former criminal with one murder already under his belt… Matt Hunter. Unwilling to lose everything for a second time, Matt and Olivia are forced outside the law in a desperate attempt to save their future together.

Hull, Wynbrandt and Lilien will serve as showrunners, writers and exec producers with Coben and Ben Coben serving as exec producers through Final Twist Productions.

The news comes six months after Coben extended his deal at Netflix, which came to life at the streamer in 2018 with the adaptation of Safe . It was followed by British series The Stranger , Polish adaptation of The Woods , the Spanish adaptation of The Innocent , the French adaptation of Gone for Good , Poland's Hold Tight and Just One Look , the British series Stay Close, Fool Me Once, Missing You, Run Away, and U.S. series I Will Find You. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Next up, is a British adaptation of The Woods and a U.S. adaptation of Myron Bolitar from David E. Kelley and Kyle Long.

Netflix's Head of UCAN Scripted Series Jinny Howe told Deadline earlier this summer that Coben "really understands his audience" and the partnership has been "very, very successful for us".

Cole Galvin, Netflix Vice President of Drama Series, who was promoted last month , said, "Harlan Coben is one of the great creative partnerships at Netflix, and The Innocent marks our 15th story together. Nobody builds a can't-look-away thriller like Harlan, and Robert Hull, Bryan Wynbrandt and Steven Lilien brought their own incredible creativity to I Will Find You , a global hit for us. We're thrilled to welcome them to the Netflix family, and we can't wait for the world to get hooked on their Innocent ."

"We're thrilled to call Netflix our home and couldn't be more grateful to our friends Jinny Howe, Cole Galvin, James Flannery, Mike Azzolino, and of course, the incredible Harlan Coben, for their continued partnership," added Hull, Wynbrandt and Lilien. "Bringing I Will Find You to life and seeing it connect with audiences around the world was an amazing experience. We're excited to bring our signature brand of twisty and propulsive storytelling to The Innocent and the many new stories we look forward to telling at Netflix."

StoryMath is represented by CAA and Range, with Lilien and Wynbrandt represented by attorney Todd Rubenstein and Hull represented by attorney Dave Ryan.

Book adaptations at Netflix are clearly working.

The company noted that Coben's I Will Find You , which was published by Grand Central Publishing, saw a 500% increase in sales after the announcement of the show.

Elsewhere, The Whisper Man , which starred Robert DeNiro, saw a similar increase in sales, Remarkably Bright Creatures saw sales across all formats rise 560% from its first-look launch to its peak in May, East of Eden , published by Penguin Classics, hit the number one on Amazon's best sellers list some 74 years after publication with a 200% rise in sales and Little House on the Prairie helped drive 110% more sales for the Storytide and HarperCollins-published book.

On screen, book adaptations account for nearly 20% of total view hours and over 13B global views since 2025, per the streamer.

The company was at the Texas Book Festival this weekend for the first time with a panel featuring The Hunting Wives author May Cobb and Guarding Stars author Katherine Center as well as Virgin River showrunner Patrick Sean Smith and exec Cole Galvin.

"People come to comfort and heartland stories for connection and optimism—the kind of story you put on to unwind. Those titles have drawn more than a billion views on Netflix since 2023, and they've reached viewers in more than 90 countries," added Galvin. "But what matters most to me are the readers who loved these books first. We work with authors and creators to honor what made the stories special, and then we invite new fans in. From Virgin River to Little House on the Prairie to Guarding Stars , our job is to give audiences more of what they love."

articles.title: Why It Was So Important The Gilded Age Jumped The Broom In This Week’s Powerful Wedding Scene
articles.summary: Audra McDonald spoke about this moment of representation.
articles.content:
Spoilers ahead for the most recent episode of The Gilded Age .

While The Gilded Age fans are concerned over Marian and Larry , Peggy and William have officially tied the knot. In a conversation with People , McDonald spoke said "it meant everything" for the series to show the new pair jumping the broom onscreen, highlighting similar opinions to her character Dorothy. In the Broadway legend's words:

For those unfamiliar, jumping the broom is a wedding ceremony that goes back antebellum period in the United States. While enslaved people couldn't legally get married, couples would jump over a broom together to symbolize their union. It's remained a tradition for Black Americans in the years that followed, continuing to this day.

Indeed, the Scott family has come a long way since Season 1 of The Gilded Age . Despite trauma and issues, Peggy and her parents have found their way back to each other throughout the last three seasons. It was actually the same broom that Dorothy and Arthur jumped over before they were able to legally marry, making Peggy's use of the ceremony a full circle moment for the entire family.

Season 4 of The Gilded Age has been changing the dynamics of various characters, and Peggy is no exception. On top of being published writer, she's now a married woman in good standing with society. Having her jump the broom honored the character's history, and also had the opportunity to educate fans who might not know about this tradition. As she the show's EP continued:

Ultimately the Kirklands ended up relenting, and Peggy and William jumping in the broom in a beautifully shot sequence of their nuptials. We'll just have to wait and see how Peggy's relationship with her in-laws changes now that they're officially family.

articles.title: What Does Robert Pattinson's James Bond Movie Mean for The Batman's Future in the DCU?
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson has been cast as the new James Bond, ending a multi-year search for actor Daniel Craig's replacement as 007. Craig ended his run with the milestone 25th Bond film, No Time to Die, and Robert Pattinson will be stepping into a whole new era (both literally and figuratively) with Bond 26. Amazon-MGM has […]
articles.content:
Of course, all the hype around Pattinson as Bond is quickly raising another big question: What does being Bond mean for Robert Pattinson's role as The Batman , and the Dark Knight's future in the DC Universe?

As Robert Pattinson gets cast as James Bond, he's also filming The Batman: Part II , the highly anticipated sequel to Matt Reeves' 2022 reboot. The Batman: Part II is slated for release on February 18, 2028, almost six full years after the first film hit theaters. Despite early rumors that The Batman: Part III could film close to the sequel, there have been no official indications that the series will continue after the second film.

One of the biggest hurdles to The Batman ‘s future has been the launch of DC Studios and the creation of a whole new DC Universe brand of interconnected TV and movie projects. James Gunn and Peter Safran were angling to introduce a new Batman (father to his son, Robin V/Damian Wayne) into the shared universe; that left Pattinson's Batman in the awkward position of being in a standalone franchise, even though a lot of fans wanted him to be part of the shared universe. Neither side seemed to budge, and the result has been the delay of any Batman movie moving forward in the last four years.

By the time The Batman: Part II comes out, it's hard to see the creative team being down for another round so soon after the ordeal of making the sequel . So is Part II really the end of the franchise? It may be for Reeves' run with the character, but it doesn't mean it will be the end for Pattinson's run as Batman.

Warner Bros. has been absorbed by Skydance-Paramount, and the company's CEO, David Ellison, has reportedly made it clear he wants Robert Pattinson's Batman to be part of the interconnected side of the DCU , alongside David Corenswet's Superman. That's been a long-held debate within the DCU fandom, and a direct echo of old debates about Christian Bale's Batman going from Christopher Nolan's universe into Zack Snyder's DCEU franchise. Half the fandom thinks that Matt Reeves built a perfect version of Batman and Gotham City that are stark contrast to James Gunn's bright and colorful version of Superman and the city of Metropolis. Other fans think Reeves' Se7en -style Batman movie has no place or purpose in the DCU .

Either way, playing James Bond doesn't stop Robert Pattinson from being the DCU Batman. If Ellison has his way , then The Batman: Part II would obviously be structured in a way that opens that franchise up to the larger DCU franchise around it. Pattinson's Batman would then be ready for an appearance in something like a Justice League team-up film as soon as 2030 or 2031 ( around the time rumors say Ellison wants the team-up film on the screen). That's the fastest track to getting Batman back to being a major draw at the movies, and a franchise staple for the DCU . Timing-wise, Pattinson could definitely make it work: in fact, the English actor could keep a pretty active and routine work schedule over the last few years, alternating between filming entire Bond movies and filming select scenes in a Justice League movie or some other kind of team-up film. It's not like one role automatically cancels out the other.

The question hanging over Pattinson's Batman being in the DCU is: would it be the same character? And would Pattinson be game? Under James Gunn and Peter Safran, there were many different kinds of DCU content, from family-friendly films like Superman to more adult-oriented fare like HBO's Lanterns or the Creature Commandos adult animated series. It remains to be seen if Ellison and new DC Studios head Jeremy Latcham are allowing that same variety in the franchise going forward.

That's really the biggest impediment to Robert Pattinson playing both Bond and Batman: the actor's own preferences and desires. Pattinson got into the franchise based on Matt Reeves' vision for the character and his world; there's nothing to suggest he would be interested in a version of Batman who is standing next to Superman, Wonder Woman, Green Lantern, and The Flash. If anything, Pattinson's last decade of role choices (including big blockbusters like Nolan's Tenet and The Odyssey , or Dune: Part Three ) suggest that he's actively avoiding big shared universe roles in franchises like Marvel, Star Wars, or even DC. So it's really hard to imagine him signing on to continue after The Batman: Part II , at this point. But then, you know: that dump truck full of money can change anyone's mind.

Robert Pattinson will return as Batman in The Batman: Part II , which has a release date of February 18, 2028.

But additional staff and voice cast have yet to be revealed.

The Guy She Was Interested In Wasn’t a Guy at All will be streaming exclusively with Crunchyroll outside of Japan when it finally makes its debut, and it will even feature Nirvana’s “Breed” as its official opening theme. With more details for the new series to be revealed ahead of its January premiere, this early look at the first episode is going to be one of the most substantial updates for the series yet. If you're in the area you'll want to look into it for sure.

The Guy She Was Interested In Wasn’t a Guy at All is a romance series that fans have been begging to see adapted ever since it made its debut back in 2022. The trailers for the anime have reached millions of hits within a very short time, and it's hard not to see why as its central duo of girls have a quite a unique path for their potential romantic connection. articles.content:
In a statement released by Amazon MGM, Pattinson opened up about taking on the role, revealing his own enthusiasm for the character. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis (Villeneuve), Amy (Pascal), David (Heyman), Tanya (Lapointe), and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

It's worth noting that even though Robert Pattinson wasn't among the early names listed as screen testing for James Bond, the actor himself has previously lobbied for the role. Back in 2012, in an interview with The Sun , the star said: “I’d definitely like to go for Bond, but in more like 20 years. There’d be nothing worse than, like, ‘Let’s get a fresh-faced Bond!’ That would be the worst idea in the world. It would be ridiculous to reinvent it as some young posh kid. After Daniel Craig, you have to have some baggage.”

To his credit, he may have been off by a bit of time, but the fourteen years since this quote, which arrived on the heels of The Twilight Saga concluding, have proven that Pattinson is a distinct performer who can not only surprise audiences but bring his weirdness and gravitas to any size production. His previous comments, mixed with his statement today, show a man who is ready to take the role.

Naturally, news that a new James Bond has been named for just the second time this century (and only the seventh time overall) has dominated the conversation online, but there's more to today's news underneath the hood than just another actor getting his next big job. As fans know, the upcoming James Bond 26 will be the first time the official franchise has not been produced by a member of the original rights holders, the Broccoli family.

Albert R. Broccoli produced the first seventeen movies in the film prior to his death, with daughter Barbara Broccoli and stepson Michael G. Wilson taking over afterward and producing every film up until 2021's No Time to Die . After Amazon acquired MGM, though, they eventually made a deal with EON Productions to assume full creative control of the Bond franchise. To that end, the studio could very well be hoping for something very different with this Bond, such as a line buried in TheWrap's report on today's news where they write that casting the role for Amazon included “the potential for the actor to also be involved in a TV spin-off.”

It's worth noting that Pattinson's career as an actor has only seen him appear in three TV productions at all, each a TV movie filmed before the Twilight movies. Even with DC, Pattinson didn't reprise his role as Batman for the TV spinoff The Penguin, either, but it's possible that Bond could command a different kind of appearance, especially if the price is right.

“Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey,” director Denis Villeneuve said of the casting.. “We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”

A production timeline for James Bond 26 has not been confirmed, with no release date set either, but both Pattinson and Villeneuve seem eager to get started.

articles.title: In Choosing Robert Pattinson, Bond Producers Have Taken the Safe Bet — But Is It the Right One? (Opinion)
articles.summary: So much for the underdog. After the race to be the next James Bond was reported to be down to three on-the-rise Brits — Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Callum Turner — Robert Pattinson crashed the conversation late in proceedings, hugely pulling focus in a matter of days. Why wouldn’t he? Suddenly, a competition of […]
articles.content:
So much for the underdog. After the race to be the next James Bond was reported to be down to three on-the-rise Brits — Jack Lowden, Josh O'Connor and Callum Turner — Robert Pattinson crashed the conversation late in proceedings, hugely pulling focus in a matter of days.

Why wouldn't he? Suddenly, a competition of next-big-things had a bona fide already-big-thing in the mix. 40 years old and known to multiplex audiences for almost half that lifetime, the Londoner is a household name who, even by his established standards, has been enjoying a banner year at the movies: sharing in the blockbuster glory of Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" this summer, sandwiched by inspired star turns in two offbeat A24 projects, "The Drama" and "Primetime," that both impressively overperformed at the box office. All that, and he's still got "Dune: Part Three" coming up next month. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues

Adding James Bond to his roster feels almost like gilding the lily, which is one reason I was skeptical that he'd ultimately be picked: Wasn't the announcement of Pattinson (along with Nicholas Hoult) as a contender just a glittery distraction to juice up public interest in a lower-profile selection process?

Shows what I know. In picking Pattinson as the next 007, the 64-year-old movie franchise is heading into unprecedented territory: Bond has traditionally been a star-making role, not one for a readymade movie star, and that has worked out more often than not. (George Lazenby, it simply wasn't meant to be.) Sean Connery had played just one leading role before he was cast in 1962's "Dr. No"; prior to donning the tux, Roger Moore and Pierce Brosnan had both found their signature roles on TV. Timothy Dalton, a reasonably seasoned and well-regarded actor when cast as Bond, never quite made the leap to stardom via the role; Daniel Craig, on the other hand, very much did. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Lowden, Turner and O'Connor all made perfect sense given this history, while Pattinson, already known to billions for playing Edward Cullen and Batman, brings associative celebrity baggage that Bond has never had to contend with before. Is that a problem? Not necessarily. Director Denis Villeneuve , a high-end, blue-chip blockbuster artist with a distinct stylistic signature, isn't the typical choice of Bond helmer either — so if he's going in his own prestigious direction with the series, it makes sense for him to take an equivalently A-list leading man (and one with whom he has an existing relationship, through "Dune: Part Three") with him.

And yet there's something about the choice, on paper at least, that doesn't sit right with me. It seems a little too neat, too convenient, even a bit too risk-averse — the proven safe bet taken over the chance to mint a brand-new megastar. I have little doubt that Pattinson, a reliably terrific actor, will make a fine Bond: tall and elegant and angularly handsome, he certainly looks the part and he can project the balance of charm and chill needed to play a character who, in any incarnation, remains a suave killing machine.

Is he a little too good for the part, though? Perhaps. Pattinson's reputation as a movie star rests on playing two darkly brooding mainstream heroes; his reputation as an actor, however, has been considerably enriched by his predilection for playing, frankly, losers and weirdos: a hapless small-time criminal in the Safdie Brothers' "Good Time"; a deranged, gull-mauling lighthouse keeper in "The Lighthouse"; a sniveling, pathetic read of Chris Hansen in "Primetime"; or whatever the hell he's doing, multiple times over, in Bong Joon-ho's loopy sci-fi "Mickey 17." Even his blockbuster assignments are more interesting when he lets his inner freak out to play: His big, heightened, leeringly villainous turn in "The Odyssey" is off on its own beam entirely.

I don't know that James Bond is really the role to mine Pattinson's most compelling eccentricities as an actor: The very point of the character, across 25 films, has been that he's a well-dressed, tightly controlled cipher who has a sharp way with a one-liner. Perhaps Villeneuve and his chosen star have other ideas, but it's hard to imagine the character straying too far from a failsafe template. One hopes instead that Pattinson is negotiating himself enough time between 007 shoots (and at least one more "The Batman" entry still on the docket) to do the odd auteur projects he clearly loves — and that adventurously chosen collaborators like Claire Denis ("High Life") and Lynne Ramsay ("Die My Love") can only benefit from his cachet. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In the meantime, spare a thought for the less famous guys who, for a moment there, thought they had a shot at being cinema's longest-running action man. They'll all be fine — I confess to some relief in particular that O'Connor, a superb and unusual hybrid of character actor and leading man, may have more time for the intrepid arthouse projects in which he thrives — and will doubtless each get some manner of boost for having been so prominently on the shortlist. Sometimes, however, the winner really does take it all in this business: For Pattinson, snagging the most in-demand role going just feels like a victory lap.

articles.title: Now That We Know Who Is Playing James Bond, Who Could Be The Next Bond Girl?
articles.summary: The prediction markets have their favorites. Who's yours?
articles.content:
The next big question on a lot of James Bond fans' minds, now that Robert Pattinson has been named the next Bond , is who will play the next “ Bond Girl ”? Though the rumors and anticipation haven’t quite reached the fevered pitch that the Bond casting rumors did, there is still plenty of speculation out there. My feeling on it is that it could be one of the frontrunners, like Sydney Sweeney or Margaret Qualley, but it’s just as likely to be a name we’ve not heard yet. With all that said, let’s get into some of the rumors.

Looking at the prediction markets like Kalshi, the leader right now to be the next Bond Girl is Margaret Qualley in the yet-untitled Bond 26 . As of today, she’s sitting at about 60% odds to nab the role. This is after coming on strong in recent weeks, after Sydney Sweeney had been the favorite for months. Sweeney’s odds have dropped to about 10% recently, but I still think she should be considered a serious contender, given her trajectory over the last few years.

The only other actresses above 20% are Ana Taylor-Joy (25%) and Florence Pugh (20%). These rumors make a lot of sense, actually. Like Pattinson, they have both worked with Bond 26 director Denis Villeneuve in the Dune series. Until just recently, Pugh wasn’t among the speculation, really, but she’s a big part of the upcoming Dune: Part III , so perhaps Villeneuve may keep the band together.

So those are the top names on the prediction markets, but could it be someone else completely? Possible. These are pure speculation on my part, but how about Inde Navarrette ? Her star is on the rise after her excellent performance in the surprise smash Obsession earlier in the 2026 movie schedule . She’s definitely someone to watch and could definitely draw some attention from the Bond producers, though she is scheduled to play Rogue in the 2028 X-Men movie, so she might not be available.

articles.content:
Speaking to The Fourth Curtain , Hudson shared some new insight into how development on Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic has been going. Although Hudson didn't provide any definitive timelines on when the game might arrive, he did say that Arcanaut Studios, which is helming the project, is working at a “very brisk pace.” He also added that much of the most important work on Fate of the Old Republic is already set in stone, mentioning that this isn't a game where the development team will have to wait until late in the project's creation to know how it might pan out.

“I mean if you talk to folks at the studio, we work at a very brisk pace,” Hudson said. “It’s, on the one hand, challenging because we set a high bar for how quickly we can move, but, then, you look at where we get to – we work in six-month cycles of big milestones every six months – and every six months we look at it and go, ‘Oh my god, like – we’ve gone so far!’ And so we’re moving quickly through things. This isn’t a project where we kind of wait around until the end to sort of figure out what we’re doing.”

As for when we might next see Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic , Hudson also confirmed that there are plans to share more of the game in 2027. Specifically, Hudson said that new details on Fate of the Old Republic should drop at some point early next year, indicating that we're mere months away from getting a new trailer or information of some sort.

“[There are] some pretty exciting things coming next year,” he continued. “So we’re going to be gradually rolling out some new announcements and information about the game, but, you know, you won’t have to wait too long into next year before we’ll have some things to share.”

Currently, Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic doesn't have a broad launch window, nor have platforms for the game been confirmed. Assuming that we do get more info on the project in 2027, though, this could be changing soon enough. Once we have more official details, we'll be sure to fill you in here on ComicBook .

articles.title: Doctor Who Tried to Launch a Spinoff Around Its Most Unexpected Character (& It Only Lasted One Episode)
articles.summary: K-9 was already one of the strangest things to come out of Doctor Who. A robotic dog with a laser built into his nose sounds like something a particularly enthusiastic toy manufacturer would dream up, but audiences loved him. So naturally, the BBC eventually decided he deserved a television show of his own. There was […]
articles.content:
The resulting pilot, K-9 and Company: A Girl's Best Friend , arrived in December 1981. It introduced a new adventure for Sarah and her mechanical companion, but the BBC never ordered a full series. That's a little surprising when you consider what happened to Doctor Who ‘s other spinoffs in the years that followed. Sarah Jane eventually got another television series, while K-9 became a franchise fixture in his own right. This first attempt at giving them their own show was left behind after a single episode.

There's a reason the BBC settled on Sarah Jane Smith and K-9 for its first proper television spinoff attempt. Elisabeth Sladen had become one of the most recognizable companions in Doctor Who history, and K-9 was an instant hit after joining the Fourth Doctor's adventures. The two had already developed a wonderful relationship on television, so bringing them together again wasn't exactly a difficult sell. The setup was rather different from the usual TARDIS adventures, though. Sarah had returned to ordinary life after leaving the Doctor, and A Girl's Best Friend introduced her living in the fictional village of Moreton Harwood. She inherited K-9 Mark III as a gift from the Doctor and soon found herself investigating a mysterious local cult. Her Aunt Lavinia was away, and Sarah also had a new housemate in Brendan Richards. It was basically a supernatural detective adventure with a journalist and a robotic dog. Honestly, that's not a terrible television premise.

The pilot also had a slightly different personality from the parent series. Instead of traveling through time and space, Sarah investigated strange goings-on in a seemingly ordinary English village. K-9 provided the familiar science-fiction element, but Sarah was very much the lead character. John Leeson returned to provide K-9's voice, while Elisabeth Sladen got the opportunity to carry a story without waiting for the Doctor to turn up and save the day. The BBC broadcast A Girl's Best Friend on December 28, 1981. It even had its own theme music, composed by Ian Levine and Fiachra Trench. There was clearly some enthusiasm behind the project. The BBC had an established character audiences already knew and a format that could have supported plenty of weekly adventures. Unfortunately, one pilot was all viewers got.

The frustrating thing about K-9 and Company is that it wasn't necessarily a bad idea. Sarah Jane was an established character with plenty of personality, and K-9 offered something that separated the proposed series from an ordinary mystery drama. But the BBC ultimately decided against ordering a full season. The pilot attracted an audience, although its reception wasn't enough to secure the series. There's also something worth remembering about the timing. Doctor Who was still going through a period of considerable change during the early 1980s. Tom Baker had recently left, Peter Davison had taken over, and the parent series was trying to establish a new era. Launching another production required money and resources that the BBC wasn't necessarily prepared to commit. Sarah and K-9 had a perfectly workable setup, but that didn't guarantee the network would take a chance on them.

Of course, the story didn't end there. Sarah Jane eventually returned to television in School Reunion in 2006, where she reunited with the Tenth Doctor and K-9. That appearance helped set up The Sarah Jane Adventures , which finally gave Elisabeth Sladen the starring series she never got in 1981. K-9 also received several attempts at becoming the star of his own adventures, including an Australian-produced series that premiered in 2009. Looking back, K-9 and Company feels like an early experiment that the franchise eventually found a way to revisit. There's something rather charming about that. The BBC had already figured out that Sarah Jane and K-9 could work together, but it took another 25 years before audiences got to see Sarah lead her own successful television adventure. I still think there's something wonderfully ridiculous about a robotic dog getting his own spinoff before the Doctor's former companions became a regular part of the franchise's television lineup. At least this time, the BBC got more than one episode out of the idea.

The Beatlemaniac might be the easiest category to shop for. More than 60 years after the Fab Four first took the world by storm, there's no shortage of new music releases, archival box sets, photo books and collectible merchandise to keep even the most devoted fans busy.

This year is particularly fruitful for vinyl collectors, with a new five-LP "Rubber Sou"l box set featuring previously unreleased studio recordings and a fresh stereo mix, alongside a special-edition pressing of Paul McCartney ‘s latest solo album, "The Boys of Dungeon Lane." There's also a new soundtrack accompanying the Wings documentary "Man on the Run," available in collectible colored vinyl editions. For fans more interested in the band's history, George Harrison's "The Third Eye: Early Photographs" features more than 200 never-before-seen photographs taken by Harrison. Meanwhile, Erika White's "Meat the Beatles : The Butcher Cover" unpacks the story behind the band's controversial 1966 "Yesterday" and "Today" album artwork, while Lennon devotees get a deluxe "Power to the People" Blu-ray box set featuring restored footage of his 1972 Madison Square Garden concerts.

Ahead, the best Beatles gifts to shop in 2026.

The Beatles' 1965 classic gets a major upgrade with this new five-LP box set, featuring a fresh stereo mix by Giles Martin and Sam Okell, previously unreleased studio recordings and the original mono and U.S. editions. An accompanying 88-page hardcover book offers a deeper look at the making of one of the band's most influential albums.

For Beatles fans who already have an extensive record collection, this special-edition pressing of "Rubber Soul" offers something a little different. The collectible LP features animated zoetrope artwork that comes to life when the record spins under the right lighting.

Paul McCartney returned with his first new solo album in more than five years in 2026, and this two-LP release includes three previously unreleased tracks and an alternate mix of his duet with former bandmate Ringo Starr.

Released alongside the 2026 documentary chronicling Paul McCartney's post-Beatles years with Wings, this soundtrack brings together music from one of the most transformative periods of his career. Collectors can choose from special-edition pressings, including an Amazon-exclusive orange vinyl and a taxi-yellow edition from Third Man Records.

Paul McCartney's post-Beatles career gets the oral-history treatment in this book chronicling the formation, success and eventual dissolution of Wings. The new 2026 paperback edition includes an additional conversation between McCartney and Morgan Neville, director of the documentary "Man on the Run."

For Beatles obsessives who know every lyric and recording session, this book offers a different way into the band's history. Authors Gary Kemp and Simon Halfon explore the extraordinary social and cultural world of manager Brian Epstein during his final year, using his personal address book to trace the people and relationships surrounding the Fab Four.

The Beatles' psychedelic world gets an unexpected collectible treatment with this model train set from British toy manufacturer Hornby. Featuring "Yellow Submarine"-inspired artwork across a miniature Eurostar.

For a more affordable holiday keepsake, these playful Beatles ornaments turn recognizable album artwork and musical imagery into miniature Christmas decorations. Designs include a "Now and Then" mixtape, "Rubber Soul"-inspired artwork and a "Yellow Submarine" drum set, with several options priced under $30.

Beatlemania gets the building-block treatment with this collectible construction set from MEGA. But act fast: the set sold out immediately upon release and is now being resold in limited quanitites on sites like Ebay.

Abbey Road Studios celebrates six decades of "Revolver" with this exclusive heavyweight cotton T-shirt. Featuring Robert Freeman's photography alongside the album's recording dates and track list, the design pays tribute to the groundbreaking 1966 sessions that helped redefine what the Beatles could achieve in the studio.

John Lennon and Yoko Ono's landmark 1972 Madison Square Garden performances get an extensive re-release in this deluxe Blu-ray collection. Featuring restored concert footage, the documentary One to One: John & Yoko and a 128-page book, the set offers a deeper look at Lennon's early solo years.

For the Beatles fan who already owns every record, coffee table book and vintage tee, "Meat the Beatles: The Butcher Cover" digs into one of the band's strangest — and most collectible — pieces of lore. Erika White. The image sparked instant outrage, a Capitol Records recall and decades of collector obsession. The new book traces the story behind the chaotic photo session led by. photographer Robert Whitaker. It doesn't ship out until November but if you pre-order it now you'll thank yourself for thinking ahead once the holidays roll around.

"The Boys of Dungeon Lane," is Beatles legend Paul McCartney's new solo album, and a highly-anticipated release for any Beatlemaniac. This limited-edition vinyl is available exclusively at Amazon and pressed in an exclusive white hue. The set includes a 12-page lyric booklet and embossed cover artwork.

"1964: Eyes of the Storm," by McCartney and historian Jill Lepore, features more than 274 largely unseen images from the legendary months between 1963-1964 when The Beatles became an international sensation — all taken on McCartney's 35mm camera. The hefty tome also includes an candid forward written by McCartney and Lepore's essay "Beatleland." Check out more pop-culture coffee table books here.

Acclaimed music anthologist and writer Philip Norman utilizes years of research and first-hand interviews with those close to the Fab Four in this expansive biography, published 11 years after the iconic rock band split up and, most notably, a year after John Lennon's assassination. The epic tale charts the English stars from their humble beginnings in Liverpool, to their astonishing heights of fame, to their acrimonious split. This edition is updated to include Paul McCartney's 1997 knighting and Lennon's 1980 assassination.

John Lennon has cited Braun's biography as the most honest account of the band's hey-day, even better than Hunter Davies' much more popular, and also very good, biographical "Beatles Book." Braun takes readers through a nothing-is-off-limits ride-along with the band-members, showcasing each musician's famous wit, even when it gets them in trouble at times.

Quality prints are a sophisticated way for music-lovers to decorate the house and showcase their taste without being ostentatious. This black-and-white Huckleberry print shows a rare photo of the four Beatles wading through a pool in 1964. Shot by John Loengard for the Life Picture Collection, it's part of a limited-edition set of 495 prints, numbered and certified with a story of the image on the back of the print.

This LEGO building kit is part puzzle, part game and part art. The set comes with pieces to build a portrait of any four of the Beatles, whose end product measures to be a 15.5″ square, to be displayed on your wall or shelf anywhere in your home.

Spread some Beatles love while on the road with this adorable Yellow Submarine decal sticker. Place it on your rearview window and you might even make friends with the car behind you while stuck in traffic.

Decorate anything from your laptop, water bottle to notebooks with these vibrant, large stickers featuring artistic images and graphics from vintage Beatles posters and magazine features. The pack comes with 24 different stickers, sized 2.5″ x 3.5″.

Any guitar player inspired by Lennon and Harrison's impressive riffs will love this collectible tin, that comes with 15 high-quality guitar picks printed with iconic Beatles imagery.

articles.title: 5 Most Outrageous Missions in Grand Theft Auto History
articles.summary: There's nothing more synonymous with Grand Theft Auto than unmitigated freedom. I'll never forget cuing up the Grand Theft Auto 3 disc on my PS2 in high school, thinking, "Wow, I can literally go anywhere and do anything." It was an incredibly overwhelming but empowering feeling, and one that Rockstar has continued to build upon […]
articles.content:
But like every ecosystem, there is an indisputable spectrum that spans from the wacky and absurd all the way up to the rigid peak of order and structure. Somewhere in between is where “societal norms” reside. Grand Theft Auto always did a great job of satirizing the spectrum, especially the more outrageous side of civilization. Between selling illicit goods, wacking the competition, and brokering deals, players would occasionally be asked to embrace hilarity and chaos or take on the darkest and most depraved tasks. Everything from breaking into a military black site to steal experimental tech to personally handling the torture of an unlucky recipient, Rockstar has repeatedly found ways to have players engage in situations they never would have imagined when first booting up the game. Let's take a look at some of the missions that made us laugh, cringe, or question what in the hell we were actually playing.

Do you remember The Truth? No, I'm not talking about some random undisclosed secret, but the wild hippie conspiracy theorist who moonlights as a marijuana farmer. When a man of such stature beckons you to break into a secret military installation known as Area 69 (subtle, Rockstar) to steal an experimental jetpack, what do you do? Well, of course, you do what he says. I mean, how could you not? As CJ, the main protagonist and player character for GTA: San Andreas , there's no reason you can't single-handedly take on the military defenses in place at such a facility.

Of course, this facility is actually an underground complex. You'll have to tackle targeting defense systems, military personnel, and all sorts of chaos and disaster. Once you find your objective, you'll be leaving with a jetpack on your back. At this point in the story, you've come a long way from neighborhood shootouts with the Ballas gang, a rival to CJ's own Grove Street crew. It feels almost surreal, like the game morphed into some twisted espionage or sci-fi adventure.

Players' first outing in Vice City is set during the 1980s. Tommy Vercetti comes to town and gets mixed up with the local criminal element. But not every paying customer is a completely crooked gangster or underboss. In fact, Tommy finds himself on the payroll for the popular (and fictitious) rock band, Love Fist. Tommy is often at their beck and call. At one point, he delivers a potent concoction of cocaine and “boomshine” known as “Love Juice” to the band. After all, if they're going to be rock stars, they have to party like rock stars. But at one point, Jezz, Willy, Dick, and Percy (see a pattern there?) attract the attention of a homicidal stalker who is hell-bent on eliminating the band. At one point, the shifty bugger dresses as a female groupie in an attempt to assassinate the band. Tommy runs him down and seemingly kills him in a thrilling chase sequence.

However, the man's vengeance is not over. He survived, and during a mission where Tommy escorts the band in a limousine, it is revealed that he's outfitted the limo with an explosive that will detonate should the speed of the vehicle drop below a particular threshold. Where's Keanu when you need him, right? Players have to keep the limo speeding through town and avoiding collisions while the band defuses the potentially explosive surprise.

Grand Theft Auto 4 famously received a fun story expansion in the form of The Ballad of Gay Tony . Supporting characters from the mainline game received some additional attention, including Luis Lopez, who became the player-controlled protagonist of this DLC. Yusuf Amir, a wealthy real estate developer and arrogant aristocrat, eventually rubs shoulders with Luis and leverages the leading man to perform outrageous tasks for him, including stealing an armed helicopter from an associate. What Yusuf wants, Yusuf gets. We're talking about a man who has lived in luxury since childhood and who continues to expend his father's fortune on sex, drugs, and the absurd.

Take this wild mission, for instance. During the “For the Man Who Has Everything” mission (aptly named), Yusuf decides that he wants a subway car as a decoration for his new Gulf property. This becomes, to be frank, one of the most ridiculous heists in Grand Theft Auto history. Luis must jump aboard the targeted train from an overpass. Without any choice in the matter, the player will enter 4- and 5-star wanted levels. The full force of the police department will be hot on your tail as you navigate to the front of the train. It's your job to then disconnect the car that will be stolen for Yusuf's property. Once you've done your job, Yusuf swoops in and whisks the car away in a helicopter. It's a rather intense mission that'll keep you on your toes to the very end.

Claude has one hell of a time in Liberty City, and his former beau, Catalina, doesn't make it any easier. Catalina is a well-known GTA antagonist first introduced in GTA III. But she also played a significant role in the game's prequel, GTA: San Andreas , where she and CJ worked together for a time, causing chaos along the West Coast. She'd eventually leave that all behind to embark on a Bonnie and Clyde lifestyle with Claude until she betrayed him for greater ambitions during the events of GTA III . Quickly, she becomes a thorn in the silent protagonist's side.

During the Kingdom Come mission provided by King Courtney, Claude is sent to pick up an Esperanto (vehicle) in the parking lot at Bedford Point. Upon arrival, Claude enters the vehicle only to find a note from Catalina alerting him to the fact that she's laid a trap for our anti-hero. She sends suicide bombers high on Spank (a fictional cocaine-like drug) to blow Claude to smithereens. It's a wild and unexpected turn during Claude's saga in Liberty City, and yet another betrayal on King Courtney's part. But the most disturbing part is that Courtney and Catalina were able to use people, hopped up on substances, to sacrifice their own skin and deliver an explosive demise to Claude.

GTA 5 contains some of the most unhinged moments in Grand Theft Auto history to date. This is partially thanks to Trevor and his penchant for impulsivity and possible psychopathy. However, during the events of GTA 5 , Michael and subsequently his cohorts Franklin and Trevor are under the FIB agency's thumb, or more specifically, Steven Haines' thumb. Haines is a man who is using his knowledge of Michael's involvement in a heist to coerce the crew into performing illicit tasks for his own gain. It's a relationship that is the foundation for many of the events that occur throughout GTA 5 .

During the “By the Book” mission, Haines invites Michael and Trevor to a warehouse where he instructs Michael to assassinate an Azerbaijani man by the name of Tahir Javan. The claim is simple: he's a known terrorist. The mission occurs in two parts. Michael must travel to the location of Javan and do the deed. But the initial location is proven to be a false lead. So, then the onus falls on Trevor, who must torture Javan's associate, Ferdinand Kerimov, to learn Javan's true location. This is where the “outrageous” and truly disturbing element comes into play. As a player taking control of Trevor, you get to perform the torture yourself. This includes waterboarding Kerimov, administering electrical shocks using a car battery, yanking teeth out with pliers, or beating the man with a wrench. It's a wild and dark twist that Trevor seems to revel in. The details are what make this sequence even more wickedly awful. Removing teeth clearly affects Kerimov's speech. You can even choose where you want to bludgeon the victim (knees, arms, stomach, etc.). It's absolutely horrific. But it's a moment that encapsulates Haines' manipulation and Trevor's depravity.

articles.content:
Yu-Gi-Oh! has officially kicked off its 30th anniversary celebration in Japan with all sorts of special new events to commemorate the occasion , and Shonen Jump is going all out with a special version of the magazine featuring some of the biggest duels from the series' past. While this new edition of the magazine is unfortunately only going to be available in Japan for now, fans can see what the fuss is all about with a special trailer showing it off. You can check it out below.

As Yu-Gi-Oh! hits its 30th anniversary milestone , the franchise is going all out in Japan. “YU-GI-OH! ART WORKS” has been revealed as a special new art exhibition showing off the late Kazuki Takahashi's original work, but no potential international plans for it have been revealed as of this time. Though the franchise did have something else for everyone to enjoy with a new anime short directed by Eri Osada for KONAMI animation with Takahiro Kagami providing the character designs, and Haruka Taira serving as art director.

Yu-Gi-Oh! will also be releasing a special digital art book in Japan later this Fall to help cement this 30th anniversary, and while there's no international release planned for that either it's yet another fun way the franchise is returning. But it doesn't beat a potential return for the anime franchise as it's perfect for a remake anime series taking it on from the very beginning. With the franchise hitting this major milestone, it would be the perfect time to bring the classic anime back to the spotlight.

Yu-Gi-Oh! made a major pivot early into its run as Kazuki Takahashi shifted away from the darker death games seen in the earliest chapters to instead focus more on the trading card game battles the franchise would then be most well known for. This has made it such a massive hit over the decades that the anime would continue with a number of different iterations with new generations of stories and main characters playing their own versions of the card game from then on.

But while Yu-Gi-Oh! has found success with all of its other future generations that followed, the original series has remained in a stasis . Outside of coming back with a movie event, Yu-Gi-Oh! The Dark Side of Dimensions , back in 2016 to celebrate its 20th anniversary, the franchise is poised and ready for another new take. Though that might be tough without Takahashi around to oversee it. Can you believe it's been 30 years of Yu-Gi-Oh ? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

But breaking with the tradition of announcing a new Bond in a glamorous, British setting in favor of social media — which is younger-skewing and distinctly global — may also give fans a hint of what to expect now that the British secret agent is in the hands of an American tech company.

articles.title: This Rare Star Wars Stormtrooper Costume Looks Nothing Like the Ones in the Movies, and That's What Makes It Special
articles.summary: You're going to need a lot of firepower if you're an imperial fascist regime determined to take over the galaxy. The Galactic Empire in Star Wars isn't shy to spend on TIE Fighters, AT-ATs, and even the planet destroying Death Star. While that's great, you'll need boots on the ground to be efficient in stamping […]
articles.content:
This set is one of only two in existence, created by Andrew Ainsworth, based on the original designs of legendary Star Wars concept artist Ralph McQuarrie. While the overall mold is similar to the Stormtrooper armor we saw in A New Hope and the rest of the original trilogy, the chrome color scheme is the most striking difference from the final version. However, it seems McQuarrie's idea of the troopers was very different from what George Lucas had in mind, as he also gave them high-tech shields, along with the franchise's most iconic weapon, the lightsaber. While the final version of the Stormtroopers were nameless grunts who couldn't hit the broad side of a barn, McQuarrie's version look like knights who would demolish the rebellion before it even began.

Just think back to how effective lightsabers have been in the Star Wars franchise, cutting through enemies like butter, thinning out numbers, and even rendering blast doors useless. Now imagine if every Stormtrooper in the Empire had one. Not only would they destroy the entire rebellion, but Luke would have not even left Tatooine. Eventually, Lucas probably decided that laser swords were too powerful to be wielded by regular soldiers, and made it so that only a small set of space wizards could use them. As for the chrome color scheme, as awesome as it would have looked, it was apparently very impractical to manufacture, especially back in 1977. However, we did get a glimpse of what it would look like thanks to Captain Phasma in 2015's The Force Awakens .

It's hard to think of Stormtroopers in any other color besides white. Sure, we've seen multiple variations over the years, like Deathtroopers and Shoretroopers, but it feels a bit wrong seeing the default Stormtrooper in anything but the traditional white. That's not to say that this chrome color scheme isn't amazing. I'd probably be saying the same thing if McQuarrie's original designs were approved. With only two of its kind in existence, this armor set gives us a glimpse at how different the Star Wars universe could have been if it wasn't for certain decisions. While it all worked out in the end, the new owner of this $16,250 suit of armor probably just found the centerpiece of their collection.

Would you have preferred if Star Wars Stormtrooper armor was chrome instead of white? Let us know in the comments!

articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Amid additional photography, Curry Barker ‘s Anything but Ghosts has brought on Matthew Lillard for a new role, Deadline has learned. Character details are being kept under wraps. Lillard joins a cast featuring Barker, Aaron Paul, Bryce Dallas Howard, Cooper Tomlinson and Violet McGraw. Tomlinson and Barker lead the film as wannabe ghost hunters who find themselves in over their heads as things spiral wildly and terrifyingly out of control. Barker is directing from a script co-written with frequent collaborator Tomlinson. The project reunites Focus Features , Blumhouse Atomic, Spooky Pictures and Divide/Conquer on the heels of his breakout horror phenomenon Obsession , which is now the top-grossing film in Focus Features' history at over $521 million worldwide. Focus, Blumhouse and Divide/Conquer are also partners on Occupant , the buzzy slasher from Josh Giuliano that releases January 15, 2027 after bowing out of TIFF. Slated for release on May 7, 2027, Anything but Ghosts is produced by Jason Blum (Blumhouse), Roy Lee & Steven Schneider (Spooky Pictures), Adam Hendricks & Greg Gilreath (Divide/Conquer), in association with Image Nation and That's a Bad Idea. Executive producers are Barker, Tomlinson and Image Nation's Ben Ross. Focus has worldwide rights on the film and Universal Pictures International will handle international distribution for the studio. Most recently seen starring in Mike Flanagan's series adaptation of Stephen King's Carrie for Amazon, Lillard will reteam with the filmmaker coming up on Rot , an indie horror film from director Alex Magistro that Flanagan is producing, as we first reported. Lillard previously worked with Flanagan on The Life of Chuck and has also recently been seen in Daredevil: Born Again and Prime Video's Cross , as well as Scream 7 . Next up, he'll be seen in Tony Gilroy's Searchlight flick Behemoth! , in theaters December 4, and James Gunn's Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow . He is repped by Verve, Strand Entertainment and Heller Law.
